agent_responses.reasoning: This design has two blocking defects that together prevent approval. First, the full card PAN and customer name are written verbatim to CloudWatch logs without any redaction or masking — this is a direct PCI-DSS violation (Requirement 3.4) and a GDPR breach vector. Second, there is no PCI scope assessment anywhere in the documentation despite the service explicitly handling raw card numbers, which means the CDE boundary, network segmentation, and compensating controls are entirely undefined. Beyond the blocking items, there are four additional high/medium concerns: no log retention policy on a log group holding PAN data; no audit logging separate from debug logging; no data residency controls documented for EU data; and no explicit statement that CloudWatch logs are encrypted at rest with a CMK. The design must be revised to redact/tokenize PAN before logging, complete a PCI scope and CDE boundary review, define a log retention policy, add tamper-evident audit logging, document residency controls, and confirm encryption at rest before this gate can be approved.

agent_responses.reasoning: The RealTime Fraud Scoring v1 design has two blocking issues that prevent approval. First, full card PANs and customer names are written to CloudWatch logs without redaction — this is simultaneously a PCI DSS violation, a GDPR/data-protection breach, and a material legal liability; it must be fixed before the design advances. Second, there is no PCI scope review documented for a service that explicitly handles card numbers, which is a mandatory governance step. Beyond the blockers, three high/medium FinOps and legal concerns exist: (1) no log retention policy on a sensitive log group, (2) no cost ceiling on autoscaling for a 5000 RPS service, and (3) no cost estimate at all in the design document, compounded by a missing egress cost model. The design must be revised to address the blocking defects and provide the missing cost and compliance documentation before re-submission to the design gate.
